content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1

We need leaves commercially available, total price <=9999. Need to find templates to break bonds.

We have a template (reaction_id 647549) that breaks amide bond: retro_smarts_template: [O;D1;H0:2]=[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[NH;D2;+0:8]-[c:9])-[c:3]1:[#7;a:4]:[#7;a:5]:[#7;a:6]:[c:7]:1>> O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])-[c:3]1:[#7;a:4]:[#7;a:5]:[#7;a:6]:[c:7]:1 . [NH2;D1;+0:8]-[c:9]

So it splits amide into acid and amine fragments. Our target has an amide linking anisole ring to heterocycle (triazine? actually nnn). So we can disconnect amide to give an aniline (the anisole ring with NH) and a carboxylic acid attached to heterocycle? Wait amide: NC(=O) attached to heterocycle (c2nnn...). The amide carbonyl attached to heterocycle carbon? Actually SMILES: ...NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3... )c2N . So amide carbonyl attached to heterocycle carbon (c2). So retro amide cleavage yields aniline (the anisole ring with NH) and acid (c2nnn...c2N) with carbonyl? Actually the acid would be O=C-? The template expects O=C attached to aromatic carbon? Might work.

We need to get precursors: Aniline part: COc1cccc(N) c1? Actually after cleavage, we get aniline with NH2? The template gives [NH2]-[c:9] as amine fragment. So amine fragment would be the heterocycle attached to NH2? Wait the template splits amide into acid (aryl carbonyl) and amine (aryl amine). In our case, the amide nitrogen is attached to anisole ring (aniline). So amine fragment would be the anisole ring with NH2? Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to anisole ring, so after cleavage, we get anisole ring with NH2 (aniline) and the acid fragment is the heterocycle carbonyl (c2nnn...). So we need anisole aniline: COc1cccc(N) c1 (para? Actually the N is at position 5 relative to OMe). So SMILES: COc1cccc(N)c1 . That's p-anisidine (4-methoxyaniline). That's commercially available.

Acid fragment: c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N with a carbonyl attached (carboxylic acid). So structure: c2nnn(... )c2N attached to C=O (carboxylic acid). So we need heterocycle with carboxylic acid. Could be synthesized via functionalization of heterocycle.

We could consider another disconnection: the heterocycle is a 1,2,4-triazine? Actually nnn pattern suggests 1,2,4-triazine? The heterocycle has an N-alkyl side chain (Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3). Also has an exocyclic NH (c2N). So we could disconnect the side chain via a benzylic amine formation (C-N bond). The side chain is a phenyl attached via CH2 to N of heterocycle? Actually Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 is a benzyl attached to heterocycle carbon (C-). So we could break that C-C bond (benzylic) via a Suzuki? But maybe easier: we can consider building the heterocycle with that side chain already attached via a SN2 on a bromomethyl phenyl.

Simplify: maybe we can propose route: Step1: Amide formation between p-anisidine and heterocycle carboxylic acid (acid). Step2: Synthesize heterocycle acid from precursor: start from 2-aminopyrimidine? Actually 1,2,4-triazine-3,5-diamine? Might be complex.

Alternative: Use template that forms amide from acid and amine (reverse). So we need acid and amine commercially.

Acid fragment: maybe we can get 5-amino-1,2,4-triazine-3-carboxylic acid? Not sure.

We could also consider disconnection at the N-alkyl side chain: break the bond between phenyl CH2 and N of morpholine-like ring (N4CC(F)C4). That is a secondary amine attached to benzyl. Could disconnect to give benzyl bromide and amine (N4CC(F)C4). The amine is a fluorinated azetidine? Actually N4CC(F)C4 is a 3-membered? Wait N4CC(F)C4 is a azetidine? N4CC(F)C4 is a four-membered ring with N and three carbons, one bearing F. That's commercially available maybe as 4-fluoropiperidine? Actually N4CC(F)C4 is N-azetidine with fluorine. Might be available.

We can search for template for C-N bond formation (alkylation). Use functional_groups_broken: "C-N single bond"? Not in list. Could use "primary amines" broken? Not.

Maybe easier: Use commercially available building blocks: p-anisidine, 5-amino-1,2,4-triazine-3-carboxylic acid (if available), 4-fluoropiperidine (or N4CC(F)C4) and 4-bromobenzyl? Actually the side chain is phenyl with para substituent CN4CC(F)C4. So we need a phenyl with that amine attached. Could be 4-(N-azetidinyl)benzyl amine? Actually the phenyl has a substituent CN4CC(F)C4 attached via CH2 to N of azetidine. So the phenyl is attached to heterocycle via CH2 (benzyl). The phenyl also has that side chain.

Thus we could assemble: start from 4-bromobenzyl chloride? Might be too many steps.

Given limit 3 steps, we need simple route: maybe use commercially available "4-(4-fluoropyrrolidin-1-yl)benzylamine"? Not sure.

Alternative: Use the whole heterocycle with side chain as a commercial building block? Might be available as a drug intermediate.

We can search for availability of the whole target fragments via is_buyable.

Let's check if p-anisidine is buyable.
